old_value: E cc_kind='stun' authored in the module (sphere-collision stun; per the module's QE-combo assumption) — i.e. E is declared an intrinsic stun source.
new_value: E requires Q (declared cc_enabler): ... [source: .../Syndra@4024662] — i.e. E carries no intrinsic stun; its stun is conditional on a Dark Sphere being present to scatter.

independent_computation.question: Does Syndra's E (Scatter the Weak) stun on its own cast, or only when it knocks a Dark Sphere into an enemy?
independent_computation.method: Read every effect branch and note line of all five Syndra abilities in the cached wiki data and search for any occurrence of a stun. Then determine what produces the entity the stun depends on.

steps.claim: E's own active applies damage + knockback only — no stun.
steps.evidence: data/champions.json -> Syndra.abilities.E[0].effects[0].description: 'Active: Syndra propels a wave of force in a cone in the target direction that deals magic damage to enemies hit and knocks them back for 400 units and up to 800 units away from Syndra based on proximity, though not through terrain.' The word 'stun' does not appear in this branch.

steps.claim: The 1.25 s stun lives exclusively in E's sphere-collision branch and is gated on a Dark Sphere being knocked back.
steps.evidence: data/champions.json -> Syndra.abilities.E[0].effects[1].description: 'Dark Spheres can be knocked back for 950 units and up to 1200 units away from Syndra based on proximity, knocking back enemies they hit over 70 units, though not through terrain. Targets hit are also stunned for 1.25 seconds, during which they are also revealed, and dealt Scatter the Weak's damage if they were not damaged by the initial cast.' The subject of 'Targets hit' is the enemies hit by the knocked-back Dark Sphere, not by the cone.

steps.claim: Exhaustive check: no other Syndra ability applies a stun, so no alternative intrinsic stun could justify the old leaf.
steps.evidence: Regex scan for /stun/i across all effect descriptions and notes of Syndra P, Q, W, E, R returns exactly two hits, both in E: the sphere-collision branch (step 2) and the Transcendent Bonus branch, which itself references the same conditional ('or if the target was hit by a pushed Dark Sphere, after the stun has ended'). W's only CC is 'All targets hit are slowed by 25% for 1.5 seconds'; E's Transcendent Bonus adds a 70% slow; Q and R apply no CC.

steps.claim: The Dark Sphere the stun depends on is produced by Q (and, secondarily, by R); W cannot create one.
steps.evidence: Q 'Dark Sphere' -> 'Active: Syndra conjures a Dark Sphere at the target location ... The Dark Sphere then remains on the ground for 6 seconds.' W 'Force of Will' -> 'Syndra telekinetically grabs the nearest Dark Sphere, enemy minion or non-epic monster' (relocates an existing sphere, creates none). R 'Unleashed Power' -> 'Syndra conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones ... The Dark Spheres will then remain on the ground next to the target's current location for 6 seconds.'

steps.claim: Therefore E is a conditional CC source whose stun requires a prior sphere-creating cast; modelling it as a cc_enabler with a declared requirement on Q is the wiki-faithful encoding, and modelling it as an unconditional cc_kind='stun' is not.
steps.evidence: Steps 1-4. The old leaf embedded the QE combo as an unstated module assumption ('sphere-collision stun') while presenting E itself as a stun source; the wiki text makes the sphere a precondition, not an assumption.

independent_computation.arithmetic_note: No numeric computation is at issue for this leaf — it is a categorical CC-classification leaf. The only numbers in the branch (1.25 s stun duration, 70-unit sphere collision radius, 950/1200-unit sphere knockback, 400/800-unit enemy knockback) are unchanged by either value and are reproduced verbatim above from the cached wiki text.
independent_computation.residual_caveat: The wiki gates the stun on 'Dark Spheres', not on Q specifically: R also conjures 3 spheres that persist on the ground for 6 s, so an R-sourced sphere could in principle be scattered by E without a Q cast. 'Requires Q' is therefore slightly narrower than the wiki's literal condition. It is nonetheless the correct enabler for a non-ultimate rotation (Q is the only non-ultimate sphere source, and W only relocates existing spheres), and the direction of the correction — the stun is conditional, not intrinsic — is unambiguously supported. This caveat does not make the new value wrong; it is a note for any future rotation that opens on R.

Collecting 80 Splinters of Wrath enhances Scatter the Weak to have an increased scatter angle and slow enemies hit by 70% for 1.25 seconds starting after the knock back ends or if the target was hit by a pushed Dark Sphere, after the stun has ended.
Active: Syndra conjures a Dark Sphere at the target location that appears after a 0.6-second delay, dealing magic damage to nearby enemies. The Dark Sphere then remains on the ground for 6 seconds.
Active: Syndra telekinetically grabs the nearest Dark Sphere, enemy minion or non-epic monster within 500 units from the target location, and holds the target near her for 5 seconds.
Active: Syndra conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones. ... The Dark Spheres will then remain on the ground next to the target's current location for 6 seconds.

(no applicable formula) — searched the full document for 'cc_kind', 'cc_enabler', 'crowd control', 'enabler', 'stun': zero matches. The formula-audit table (Section 5) covers mitigation, penetration, growth, AS, haste, renewal scheduling, DoT partition, proc counting, crit expectation, shields, grey health, revive and BIS scoring, but declares nothing about crowd-control classification. This leaf is therefore adjudicated on cached wiki text alone.

verdict_rationale: The cached wiki text places the 1.25 s stun solely in E's Dark-Sphere-collision branch; E's own cone applies damage and a knockback and nothing else, and no other Syndra ability stuns. An unconditional cc_kind='stun' on E (old value) asserts CC the ability does not have on its own and silently hard-codes the QE combo as a module assumption. Declaring E a cc_enabler whose stun requires a sphere-producing cast (Q) reproduces the wiki's stated precondition and makes the previously implicit assumption checkable.
